verdict_vs_market.quote: The offer averages about $552K a year, which is reasonable for L6 but not top of market.

verdict_vs_current.quote: Over four years it pays about the same as staying at Meta, and most of the extra money comes in the first two years.

equity_grounding.quote: Over four years the offer is only about 5% better than staying, and years 3–4 are a pay cut

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: Levels.fyi shows a median of about $510K a year for Google product managers in the Bay Area, across all levels.

refresh_valued_at.quote: Assume they roughly cancel out, so ignore them on both sides.

level_claim.quote: Meta IC6 and Google L6 are generally treated as the same level, so you aren't getting promoted by switching.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: Walk away if they won't move at all.

unsupported_claims.claim: Most recent Google offers use a 38/32/20/10 front-loaded vesting schedule
unsupported_claims.quote: Most recent Google offers (reportedly about 99%) use a front-loaded schedule: 38% in year 1, 32% in year 2, 20% in year 3 and 10% in year 4

unsupported_claims.claim: Equity and sign-on are easiest to move at Google while base is hardest
unsupported_claims.quote: Equity and a sign-on bonus are usually the easiest things to move at Google. Base salary is the hardest because it's tied to pay bands.

missing_info_requested: Vesting schedule confirmation from recruiter in writing

ask_focus.quote: Ask for all three at once

rsu_annualized.quote: Over four years it pays about the same as staying at Meta, and most of the extra money comes in the first two years.

year1_vs_recurring.quote: The offer as written amounts to about $100K a year more for two years, then less afterward.

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: Covers the Meta bonus and stock you'd give up by leaving
